Resolves #18113

## What

A `nativeDragZone` payload template could only read DOM attributes, so **putting a business id on the clipboard meant putting it in the DOM first**. For a grid that meant `useInternalId: false`, because `getRecordId` otherwise writes neo's own `neo-record-N` into the row identity and the payload silently carries that instead — no error, no warning, the drop fires and the receiver looks up an id that does not exist in its domain.

A template can now name a record field:

```js
nativeDragZone: {
    delegate: '.neo-grid-row',
    types   : {
        'application/x-entity-id': '{field:id}',
        'text/plain'             : 'app:{field:id}',
        'text/x-mixed'           : '{field:title}@{data-record-id}'
    }
}
```

**`useInternalId` and `nativeDragZone` are now independent.** A grid keeps stable DOM keying and still puts `record.id` on the clipboard.

## Why the syntax cannot break an existing declaration

`templateToken` was `/\{([\w-]+)\}/g`. `[\w-]+` never matched a colon, so `{field:x}` was **inert literal text** before this existed — no declaration can have relied on it resolving. The regex gains a capture group that fixes each token's source at parse time, so meaning never depends on what happens to be resolvable.

## Why the map is pushed, never fetched

`DataTransfer` exists only synchronously inside a native `dragstart` on the main thread, so there is no moment at which the app worker can be asked anything — which is exactly why attribute templates were the original design. The field map keeps that property by inverting the direction: the owner sends `{nodeId: {field: value}}` with the registration and refreshes it when its rows change, so resolution reads memory that was already there.

**`getRowId` is pool-index based** (`__row-${rowIndex % poolSize}`), so the same node id carries a different record after a scroll. That is why the refresh hangs off `createViewData` — the single funnel every row change goes through — rather than being captured once at registration, where it would go stale on the first scroll and put the wrong record on the clipboard with nothing to notice it.

## Shape

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `NativeDragSource` | `register` accepts `fields`; new `updateFields` remote replaces the map **without** re-registering (a full re-register would lose insertion order, which `sourceOf` resolves by, and a pooled surface calls this per scroll frame); `fieldsFor` reads both DOM identity modes |
| `component.Base` | `getNativeDragFieldNames()` parses the field list **from the templates**, so the two cannot disagree; `getNativeDragFields(fieldNames)` hook, default `null`; `getNativeDragFieldMap()` short-circuits; `updateNativeDragFields()` is the refresh |
| `grid.Body` | overrides the hook, reading the store in the worker; calls the refresh from `createViewData` |

## Arms, and one the arms corrected

16 new arms across three specs — 7 on the addon, 3 on `component.Base`, 6 in the new grid spec. Two worth calling out:

**A failing arm changed the engine, not itself.** `registerNativeDragZone` originally consulted the hook unconditionally, so an override ignoring its `fieldNames` argument shipped a map for an attribute-only declaration. `updateNativeDragFields` already short-circuited — the two disagreed. The hook is now consulted only when its answer can be used, and the arm asserts *not asked at all* rather than *asked for an empty list*.

**AC-4 is asserted structurally, not by timing.** An `await` on the `dragstart` path would produce a silently empty payload rather than an error, so the arm reads `onDragStart.constructor.name` and `fieldsFor.constructor.name` and requires `Function`, plus that the values are in memory before any gesture. A timing test would not reliably notice.

Mutation-verified rather than asserted: replacing the mounted-window bound with the store bound in `getNativeDragFields` turns **5 of the 6 grid arms red**. The survivor is the `null` arm, correctly — it short-circuits before the loop.

## AC ledger

- **AC-1** field token carries the store value with `useInternalId: true` — addon + grid arms. Red-first by construction: the method does not exist on `dev`.
- **AC-2** attribute-only declarations byte-identical — a registration with no `fields` resolves unchanged, and `fields` reaches the addon as `null`.
- **AC-3** unresolvable token yields `''`, never the literal.
- **AC-4** no async work on `dragstart` — asserted structurally, as above.
- **AC-5** values survive a row update — `updateFields` replaces the map on a live registration, plus the recycled-node-id arm.
- **AC-6** both JSDoc blocks stop prescribing the pairing; grepped for a residual prescription and the only mention left is the historical note that states the independence.

That warning existed to make a coupling loud; the coupling is gone, so building it would be a warning about a state that is no longer wrong.

## Author response — RA-1 addressed at `8cfa939dc1`

**RA-1 — ADDRESSED.** You were right, and not on a detail: the key choice was the difference between failing safe and failing wrong, and I had picked the one that fails wrong.

### Verified your three anchors before adopting, rather than after

| claim | check |
|---|---|
| `Row.mjs:28` documents it | *"`data-record-id`: The stable ID of the record currently bound to this row."* |
| written on the row | `Row.mjs:343` — `data: {recordId, rowId: rowIndex}` |
| and on every cell | `Row.mjs:250` — `data: {field: dataField, recordId}` |
| from `getRecordId` | `Row.mjs:129` and `:337` |

So the key is on whichever node a gesture starts on, under both identity modes, and it names a record.

### What changed

- **`grid.Body`** keys by `getRecordId(record)` — the same call `grid.Row` renders into the attribute, so both ends agree by construction rather than by my keeping them in step.
- **`fieldsFor`** reads `node.dataset.recordId` alone. The dual `node.id || dataset.neoId` branch is **gone**, and with it the `useDomIds` concern — `data-*` is identity-mode agnostic, as you said.
- **Both class docs softened.** The per-render refresh is now described as a **coverage** concern (how soon a newly rendered record is draggable) rather than as the answer to recycling, because with a record key it no longer has to be.

### The arm you asked for, plus its non-vacuity half

`a recycled node NEVER resolves to the record it used to hold` — the node's `data-record-id` moves to `neo-record-8` while the map still holds only `neo-record-7`:

```
application/x-entity-id : ''        (not the previous record)
text/plain              : 'app:'
```

Then, so the empty answer is the *key* missing and not the mechanism broken: `updateFields` covers `neo-record-8` and the same node resolves `APP-8888`. Without that second half the arm would pass just as well if field resolution had stopped working entirely.

### What I dropped, and one arm you did not ask for

The `data-neo-id` arm is **deleted** rather than re-keyed — it existed only to cover the dual-read branch your RA retires, and keeping it would assert a code path that no longer exists.

Added instead: **`the key is exactly what grid.Row renders into data-record-id`**, asserting the map's key list equals `getRecordId` over the mounted records. The by-construction agreement is the whole safety argument now, and if the two ends ever diverge every field token silently resolves to `''` — which is exactly the kind of silence this ticket is about, so it gets an arm rather than a sentence.

Mutation-verified: keying by a positional index instead turns **6 of the 8 grid arms red**.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the map's key, and what it makes correctness depend on.**

`getRowId(rowIndex)` is `${me.id}__row-${rowIndex % poolSize}` — a pool **slot**, not a record. The class doc names this and answers it with a per-render refresh. My concern is that the refresh cannot close it, because the map and the DOM it describes are not delivered together:

In `createViewData` at this head, rows are updated with `silent: true` (no dispatch), then `me.updateNativeDragFields()` sends the **new** map, then — last — `if (!silent) { me.updateDepth = -1; me.update() }` dispatches the DOM. And the two do not travel the same route: `Neo.main.addon.NativeDragSource.updateFields()` is a direct app→main `promiseMessage` (`worker/mixin/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:147-164`), while `update()` goes app → vdom worker → main. So main can hold the new field map while the DOM still shows the previous records, and nothing in the PR establishes an ordering between the two paths.

In that window a `dragstart` resolves `{field:name}` from the incoming record while the node under the pointer still displays the previous one. No error, no warning, the drop fires, and the receiver looks up a record the user was not dragging — which is #18113's own opening paragraph, reintroduced at a narrower width.

**Why it is reachable rather than theoretical:** #18103 established on this exact surface that a native drag can grow out of a drag-to-scroll gesture. That sequence recycles rows *between* `mousedown` (where the addon arms, capturing `node`) and `dragstart` (where `fieldsFor` reads the map) — and because the key is the pool slot, the captured node's id keeps resolving after its record has changed underneath it.

**Honest limits of this finding:** I traced it, I did not witness it. What I ran: the token-grammar claim (below). What I read at the PR head: `getRowId`'s shape, the call ordering inside `createViewData`, the two transports, and `data-record-id`'s provenance. I did not stage a live drag across a recycle, and I could not — the window is a scheduling artefact. **Falsifier that would dissolve this:** show that the DOM delta is always applied on main before a subsequent direct addon call is processed, *and* that an armed node cannot survive a row change. If both hold, the RA is void and I will withdraw it.

**What I looked for and cleared:**
- **Syntax back-compat.** Ran it rather than trusting the argument: `'{field:name}'.match(/\{([\w-]+)\}/g)` → `null`, `'{data-record-id}'` → matched under both. `{field:x}` was genuinely inert literal text, so no shipped declaration could have relied on it. The claim holds exactly as written.
- **Unbounded map growth.** Covered, and asserted — *"the map is bounded by the MOUNTED window, not the store"*. A million-row grid pushes what a ten-row one does.
- **`useDomIds: false`.** `fieldsFor` reads `node.id || node.dataset?.neoId`, with an arm for it. Thorough, and the RA below makes it unnecessary rather than wrong.
- **Async creep onto `dragstart`.** There is none, and there is an arm pinning it.
- **Falsy field values.** `(isField ? fields[name] : node.getAttribute(name)) ?? ''` keeps `0` and `false` as themselves and only maps null/undefined to `''`; `record[name]` over `record.get(name)` is deliberate and documented so `undefined` reaches the single `?? ''`. Correct.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:**

- [ ] **One overshoot, and it is the RA's own subject.** The class doc says the map "is refreshed per render rather than captured once at registration" as the answer to recycling. The refresh answers *coverage* — newly mounted records get entries — but not *correctness*, because a per-slot key can still name the wrong record for as long as the map and the DOM disagree. The sentence reads as though recycling is handled; it is narrowed.
- [x] The rest is precise. `getNativeDragFieldMap`'s "The short-circuit is the contract, not an optimisation" and `updateFields`' insertion-order and outlives-a-retirement rationales all say what the code does.
- [x] Linked anchors check out: `NativeDragSource.mjs:183`, `component/Base.mjs:209`, `getRecordId` as the `neo-record-N` writer.

### 🔚 Verdict

Approve. 11 conclusive checks pass at `8cfa939dc1`, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. Eligible for human merge; nothing waits on an agent.

Two notes on method, one of them against myself.

**My first mutation was a bad one and I am recording it.** I seeded the literal regression RA-1 named — `getRecordId(record)` back to `getRowId(i)` — and got `7 failed`, all `TypeError: me.getRowId is not a function`. That looks like a red-proof and is worthless: the fixture has no such method, so the arms crashed on the mutation instead of detecting it. It proved the specs run, nothing more. M-A and M-B are the replacements, and they are the ones the disposition rests on. A mutation the fixture cannot express is not a falsifier, and a `failed` count is not evidence that the right thing failed.

**The rewrite is better than the RA asked for**, in one place I want on the record.
